record.context_brief: Geometric properties invariant under tiling equivalence
record.original_question: Classify the geometric properties P of tilings that are inherited by every tiling in the same equivalence class under mutual local derivability, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism. The motivating examples in the paper are properties such as bounded-displacement equivalence to a lattice, bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice, and linear repetitivity.

evidence.quote: Two point sets in Rd are bounded displacement equivalent (abbreviated BD) if there is a bijection between them which moves every point by at most some finite amount. Two point sets in Rd are bi-Lipschitz equivalent (abbreviated BL) if there is a bi-Lipschitz bijection between them.

A pattern Y ⊆ Rd is linearly repetitive (abbreviated LR) if there exists a constant C > 0 such that, for every r ≥ 1, every patch of size r which occurs anywhere in Y, occurs in every ball of radius Cr in Rd. The abbreviation MLD stands for mutually locally derivable.
Problem 2.7.1. Classify tilings with such a property that any other tiling MLD (or topologically conjugate, or homeomorphic) to it also has that property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Work in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$. A tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a covering of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by closed sets ("tiles") with pairwise disjoint interiors, drawn from a finite collection of prototypes up to translation. To each tiling $T$ one associates its set of control points (e.g., centers of tiles), giving a Delone (uniformly discrete and relatively dense) point set $Y_T \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.

(1) Two Delone sets $Y_1, Y_2 \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ are bounded-displacement equivalent (BD) if there exists a bijection $\phi : Y_1 \to Y_2$ and a constant $K < \infty$ such that $\|\phi(x) - x\| \le K$ for every $x \in Y_1$.

(2) $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ are bi-Lipschitz equivalent (BL) if there exists a bi-Lipschitz bijection $\phi : Y_1 \to Y_2$.

(3) A pattern $Y \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is linearly repetitive (LR) if there exists $C > 0$ such that, for every $r \ge 1$, every $r$-patch of $Y$ that occurs anywhere in $Y$ also occurs in every ball of radius $Cr$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

(4) Two tilings $T_1, T_2$ are mutually locally derivable (MLD) if there exists $R > 0$ such that the patch of $T_1$ in any ball $B_R(x)$ determines the tile(s) of $T_2$ at $x$, and vice versa.

(5) The continuous hull (tiling space) $\Omega_T$ is the closure of the translation orbit $\{T - v : v \in \mathbb{R}^d\}$ in the local (tiling) topology; $\mathbb{R}^d$ acts on $\Omega_T$ by translation. Two tilings $T_1, T_2$ are topologically conjugate if there is an $\mathbb{R}^d$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Omega_{T_1} \to \Omega_{T_2}$, and homeomorphic if $\Omega_{T_1}$ and $\Omega_{T_2}$ are homeomorphic.

Problem. Give a classification of geometric properties $P$ of tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are invariant under each of the equivalence relations on tilings induced by (a) MLD, (b) topological conjugacy of tiling spaces, and (c) homeomorphism of tiling spaces. That is, characterize those properties $P$ such that whenever a tiling $T$ has $P$ and $T'$ is MLD to $T$ (respectively, topologically conjugate to $T$, respectively, has homeomorphic tiling space), then $T'$ also has $P$. Sample properties to be tested against the resulting classifications include: BD-equivalence of $Y_T$ to a lattice, BL-equivalence of $Y_T$ to a lattice, and linear repetitivity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad classification question about which geometric properties of tilings descend to entire MLD / topological-conjugacy / homeomorphism classes. Standard references on tiling dynamics (Solomyak's notes, Sadun's surveys, the Bielefeld Tilings Encyclopedia, and Clark–Sadun "When shape matters") record specific invariance results (e.g. linear repetitivity is MLD-invariant; certain shape deformations preserve topological conjugacy class) but no general classification of such properties is reported. The question therefore appears to remain open in its general form, with only partial results known for individual properties.

status_evidence.title: Tilings Encyclopedia | MLD
status_evidence.snippet: Defines MLD as mutual local derivability; discusses how MLD induces a finer equivalence than topological conjugacy of tiling spaces.
status_evidence.claim: MLD and topological conjugacy give distinct equivalence relations on tilings, motivating questions about which properties they preserve.

status_evidence.title: When shape matters: deformations of tiling spaces — Clark & Sadun
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which shape deformations of tiles produce MLD or topologically conjugate tiling spaces, isolating specific invariants rather than a full classification.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial invariance results are available; no general classification of MLD/conjugacy/homeomorphism invariant properties is given.

status_evidence.title: Tilings and Dynamics — Solomyak (lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of tiling dynamics including linear repetitivity and MLD; treats invariance of specific properties without giving a complete classification.
status_evidence.claim: Linear repetitivity and similar properties are known to be MLD-invariant in specific cases, but a general classification scheme is not provided.
